_comment: Checks in common/dev/verify.mjs that are known to fail, each with why. A failure NOT listed here fails CI; a listed check that starts passing fails CI too (under VERIFY_STRICT_BASELINE, which the workflow sets), so this list has to shrink as things are fixed. It describes the CI environment — ubuntu-latest, the pinned Chrome — so regenerate it from a CI run rather than from a laptop: node common/dev/verify.mjs --update-baseline. A couple of these are timing-sensitive and a loaded laptop fails others besides; locally, treat an unlisted failure as information rather than as a verdict.

known.downloading a session writes every file: The SD-transfer block breaks when a link CRC is on, and only then: with VERIFY_CRC=0 every one of these passes. Not diagnosed past that. The failure shape moves between runs (a 0xc1 list-response timeout, a part-written file, a transfer that reports Failed), so the whole block is listed rather than picked over. The two sibling defects in the same interaction ARE fixed and their checks now pass, which is the evidence that this one is real and not an environment quirk: the factory-test capture used to transcribe the ACK's CRC trailer as report text, and the Shimmer3R framer could not size the ExG register reply. Tracked as DEV-1002.

known.UI recovers after the drop: Fails in CI and passes locally. The check reads the page's state a fixed 1.5 s after a simulated cable pull, and on a loaded runner the disconnect handling has not finished settling by then. The behaviour is right; the wait is a sleep where it should be a condition. Fix the check, not the page.
